findings.problem: Except deadline and a weak post-run row-count check, negative cases pass for any nonzero subprocess result with no successful journal. An unrelated syntax/import/runtime error can qualify malformed-output, missing-owner, second-output-mismatch and other controls without reaching the intended branch. Positive control only validates its own fixture and cannot rule out case-specific construction defects.
findings.required_fix: Define per-case expected failure phase, exception type/reason and adapter source location. Assert expected invocation directory count and journal check count. second-output-mismatch must have two captured rows and numerical replay changed. Output/process refusals require one captured row and exact intended reason/location; preguard refusals require zero invocation directories/checks. Pre-module guards require matching traceback assertion location and no new journal. Retain raw traceback/output and assertion evidence in each row.

findings.problem: Tracked owner replacement makes git status dirty, so the post-run guard rejects at cleanliness before owner hash equality. This proves a postguard refusal but does not independently prove post-execution owner-digest validation.
findings.required_fix: Label this case post-run-dirty-owner refusal. If claiming owner-digest postguard coverage, add a distinct synthetic case that modifies and commits the owner, then adjusts the protocol owner-head binding only through a separately frozen fixture design that isolates the digest branch; simpler, constrain claims to the actual reached cleanliness branch. Do not mutate historical evidence.

nonblocking_observations: The unchanged adapter is copied byte-for-byte; physical fixture roots match its hardcoded sibling layout. The synthetic runner and one-marker runtime are explicitly distinguished from generated-runner/scientific evidence.
Protocol mutations occur after a retained pre-mutation copy and digest. Existing journal bytes are checked for preservation. Distinct directories and no-overwrite behavior preserve control artifacts.
A source/runtime binding dictionary control is improved by actual fixture Git/file/runtime guards, once branch-specific rejection is demonstrated.
Do not state this suite proves OS sandboxing, full runtime closure, trusted freeze chronology, native correctness, PRNG distribution, OU dynamics, or Issue61 acceptance.

suggested_branch_contracts.positive: return0, complete/passed, exactly two checks and two invocation dirs, identical stable digest
suggested_branch_contracts.second-output-mismatch: nonzero, exactly two journal checks, first comparison passed, second captured output independently valid, failure_reason AssertionError: numerical replay changed
suggested_branch_contracts.deadline: TimeoutExpired or ProcessGroupTimeout exact class from owner supervisor, no completed check row, invocation1 exists, deadline elapsed bounded, retained failure journal
suggested_branch_contracts.post-run-owner-replacement: one captured row with return0/output valid, failure at guards git cleanliness after runner mutation
suggested_branch_contracts.malformed-output: one check row, JSONDecodeError at checker.strict_json, actual malformed output retained
suggested_branch_contracts.extra-output/symlink-output/missing-outp: one check row, source location at output membership/symlink assertions; physical output shape matches injection
suggested_branch_contracts.nonzero/stderr: one check row, original returncode7 or nonempty stderr respectively, failure_reason nonzero exit or stderr
suggested_branch_contracts.replacement/missing guards: zero runner invocation dirs; exact guard expression or error type/path identifies intended missing/replaced member
suggested_branch_contracts.preexisting-invocation: FileExistsError at directory.mkdir, journal failure retained, preexisting directory untouched
suggested_branch_contracts.preexisting-journal: initial journal assertion traceback and original bytes preserved
